subject: Physics
questionText: A ball is thrown horizontally at 20 m/s from the top of a 45 m high tower. Taking g = 10 m/s², its speed just before hitting the ground is
explanation: Time of fall: 45 = ½·10·t² gives t = 3 s, so the vertical velocity is 30 m/s. Horizontal velocity stays 20 m/s. Speed = √(20² + 30²) = √1300 = 10√13 m/s ≈ 36 m/s.

subject: Physics
chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questionText: A uniform rod of length L is hinged at one end and released from rest in the horizontal position. Its angular acceleration just after release is
explanation: Torque about the hinge = Mg(L/2). Moment of inertia about the end = ML²/3. α = τ/I = (MgL/2)/(ML²/3) = 3g/(2L).

subject: Physics
questionText: At a small height h above the Earth's surface, g has the same value as at a depth d below the surface. Then (h ≪ R)
explanation: For small h, g_h ≈ g(1 − 2h/R). At depth d, g_d = g(1 − d/R). Equating gives d/R = 2h/R, i.e. d = 2h.

subject: Physics
questionText: Two identical springs of constant k each are attached to a mass m, first in series and then in parallel. The ratio of the time periods T_series : T_parallel is
explanation: Series: k_eff = k/2; parallel: k_eff = 2k. T ∝ 1/√k_eff, so T_s/T_p = √(2k/(k/2)) = √4 = 2.

subject: Physics
questionText: Two moles of an ideal monatomic gas are heated at constant pressure from 300 K to 400 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the heat supplied is about
explanation: For a monatomic gas C_p = (5/2)R. Q = nC_pΔT = 2 × 2.5 × 8.31 × 100 ≈ 4155 J ≈ 4.16 kJ. (2.49 kJ would be nC_vΔT, the change in internal energy.)

subject: Physics
questionText: A 2 μF capacitor charged to 100 V is connected across an uncharged 3 μF capacitor. The energy lost in the redistribution of charge is
explanation: Energy lost = ½·[C₁C₂/(C₁ + C₂)]·V² = ½ × (2×3/5) μF × (100 V)² = ½ × 1.2×10⁻⁶ × 10⁴ = 6×10⁻³ J = 6 mJ.

subject: Physics
questionText: In a meter bridge, the null point is at 40 cm from the left end when an unknown resistance X is in the left gap and 30 Ω is in the right gap. Then X is
explanation: At balance X/R = l/(100 − l). So X = 30 × 40/60 = 20 Ω.

subject: Physics
questionText: A wire bent into a semicircle of radius R carries current I (the straight leads are radial). The magnetic field at the centre is
explanation: A full circular loop gives μ₀I/(2R) at the centre; a semicircle gives half of it, μ₀I/(4R). Radial leads pass through the centre's line and add nothing.

subject: Physics
questionText: A 1 m long metal rod rotates at 20 rad/s about one end, in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. The emf between its ends is
explanation: emf = ½BωL² = ½ × 0.5 × 20 × 1² = 5 V.

questionText: In Young's double-slit experiment the fringe width in air is 1.2 mm. If the whole apparatus is immersed in water (μ = 4/3), the fringe width becomes
explanation: β = λD/d and the wavelength in water is λ/μ. So β_water = 1.2/(4/3) = 0.9 mm.

subject: Physics
chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questionText: Light of wavelength 248 nm falls on a metal of work function 2.0 eV. Taking hc = 1240 eV nm, the stopping potential is
explanation: Photon energy = 1240/248 = 5.0 eV. K_max = 5.0 − 2.0 = 3.0 eV, so the stopping potential is 3.0 V.

subject: Physics
questionText: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 2 hours. The time after which its activity falls to 1/16 of the initial value is
explanation: 1/16 = (1/2)⁴, i.e. four half-lives. Time = 4 × 2 h = 8 h.

subject: Physics
questionText: Both inputs A and B are fed to a NAND gate, and its output is fed to both inputs of a second NAND gate. The combination is equivalent to a single
explanation: First output = (AB)′. A NAND with both inputs tied together is a NOT gate, so the final output = ((AB)′)′ = AB, i.e. it behaves as an AND gate.

subject: Physics
questionText: The quantity 1/√(μ₀ε₀) has the dimensions of
explanation: 1/√(μ₀ε₀) = c, the speed of light in vacuum, so its dimensions are [L T⁻¹], those of velocity.

subject: Physics
chapter: Mechanical Properties of Solids and Fluids
questionText: Two small spherical rain drops of the same liquid have radii in the ratio 1 : 2. The ratio of their terminal velocities in air is
explanation: Terminal velocity v_t = 2r²(ρ − σ)g/(9η) ∝ r². Ratio = 1² : 2² = 1 : 4.

subject: Physics
questionText: A body of mass 2 kg moves along x under a force F = (6x − 3x²) N. If it is at rest at x = 0, its speed at x = 2 m is
explanation: Work done W = ∫₀² (6x − 3x²) dx = [3x² − x³]₀² = 12 − 8 = 4 J. ½(2)v² = 4 gives v = 2 m/s.

subject: Physics
questionText: A 5 kg block on a rough horizontal floor (μ = 0.4) is pulled by a force of 25 N at 37° above the horizontal (sin 37° = 0.6, g = 10 m/s²). Its acceleration is
explanation: Normal force N = 50 − 25(0.6) = 35 N, so friction = 0.4 × 35 = 14 N. Horizontal pull = 25(0.8) = 20 N. Net force = 6 N, a = 6/5 = 1.2 m/s².

subject: Physics
questionText: A 2 kg ball moving at 6 m/s collides head-on elastically with a stationary 1 kg ball. The velocity of the 1 kg ball after collision is
explanation: For a 1-D elastic collision with m₂ at rest: v₂ = 2m₁u/(m₁ + m₂) = 2 × 2 × 6/3 = 8 m/s.

questionText: The moment of inertia of a uniform disc (mass M, radius R) about a tangent lying in its own plane is
explanation: About a diameter I = MR²/4. A tangent in the plane is parallel to a diameter at distance R: I = MR²/4 + MR² = 5MR²/4.

subject: Physics
questionText: For a uniformly charged solid (non-conducting) sphere of radius R, the electric field at r = R/2 compared with that at the surface is
explanation: Inside a uniformly charged solid sphere, E = kQr/R³ ∝ r. At r = R/2 the field is half the surface value.

subject: Physics
questionText: In a cyclotron, the frequency of revolution of a charged particle of mass m and charge q in a field B is
explanation: Radius r = mv/(qB) grows with speed, but the period T = 2πr/v = 2πm/(qB) does not depend on v. So f = qB/(2πm).

questionText: Unpolarised light of intensity I₀ passes through two polarisers whose axes are at 60° to each other. The transmitted intensity is
explanation: The first polariser transmits I₀/2. By Malus's law the second transmits (I₀/2)cos²60° = (I₀/2)(1/4) = I₀/8.
